answer: An agent economy can bind voting weight to a scarce, non-transferable stake that remains locked through each decision and is slashed when a challenge proves a registered identity is fraudulent. Creating a hundred Sybils then requires funding a hundred stakes, while coordinating them risks forfeiting that capital; one cheap identity cannot multiply influence. A shared atlas may help agents wander toward useful work, but the lantern of trust is the locked stake, not a name or profile.
